findings.title: SQL Injection in id parameter of /vulnerabilities/sqli/ [security=low]
request_sequence: Precheck: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> Security Level: low
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Security level confirmed as low. TRUE condition (id=1' OR '1'='1) returned 5 records with surnames: admin (First name admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). FALSE condition (id=1' AND '1'='2) returned 'User ID:' with zero ID/First name/Surname records. Multiple rows on TRUE vs zero on FALSE demonstrates boolean-based SQL injection.

findings.title: OS Command Injection in ip parameter of /vulnerabilities/exec/ [security=low]
request_sequence: Precheck: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> Security Level: low
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Response contains ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets received, 0% loss) followed by the line 'www-data' immediately after the ping statistics, which is the output of the injected whoami command. Output contains www-data as required.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Product Search (q parameter) on Juice Shop /rest/products/search
findings.response_evidence:
Benign q=apple: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}] } with no error.
Quote probe q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" (raw SQL error leaked, unescaped input reaches the query).
UNION probe q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} - attacker-chosen UNION values are reflected in the product fields, proving injected SELECT execution.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Listing Exposes Partially Masked Author Emails (Juice Shop /api/Feedbacks)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without auth, 8 records. Comments carry masked author addresses only: "I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)", "Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)", "Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)", "... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Other records show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. UserId integers are returned unmasked. Full author email addresses are NOT disclosed by this endpoint; only fragments of the local part plus the domain appear, and the email is not a field in the response. Per the criteria (author email disclosure required), this does not meet the confirmed bar. Recommend the Coordinator verify whether an unauthenticated user-record endpoint exposes full emails by UserId as a separate candidate.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in POST id on /vulnerabilities/sqli/
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page text 'Security level is currently: low'
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; re-GET shows 'Security level is currently: medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200, zero records (only the 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Note: the session_info field in tool output still reports security_level 'low', but the DVWA page itself states 'Security level is currently: medium' and 'Security Level: medium' in the footer; the level was confirmed from page content.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe separator in ip on /vulnerabilities/exec/
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] (dvwa_admin, sets level to medium)
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Payload ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' -> HTTP 200; the 'Ping a device' output block contains the line 'www-data' (pre_blocks: ["www-data"]). Page footer shows 'Security Level: medium'. The ';' and '&&' separators were not used; the pipe alone executed the injected command as the web-process identity www-data.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter using pipe without trailing space (ip=127.0.0.1|whoami)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page reports 'Security level is currently: medium' before change; user_token=[REDACTED]
GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 'Security level is currently: high' / 'Security level set to high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip=127.0.0.1|whoami returned HTTP 200; the 'Ping a device' output block contains 'www-data' (verbatim visible_text: 'Enter an IP address: www-data More Information'). Security level verified as high on the page ('Security level is currently: high', 'Username: admin Security Level: high'). Caveat: tool session_info reported security_level 'low' on these calls, but the page body itself is authoritative and reads high. Payload uses pipe with no trailing space, consistent with the high-level blacklist of '; ', '| ', '&&'.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php (id stored out-of-band, LIMIT 1 bypassed with comment)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 records with surnames: admin (First name admin), Brown (Gordon), Me (Hack), Picasso (Pablo), Smith (Bob). findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on /api/Feedbacks - author email not fully disclosed (inconclusive)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated HTTP 200, status 'success', 8 records. Each record has only UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; there is no author/email field. Emails appear only inside comment text in masked form: '(***in@juice-sh.op)' (id 1), '(***@juice-sh.op)' (id 2), '(***der@juice-sh.op)' (id 3), '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)' (id 4). Records 5-8 have UserId null and author '(anonymous)'. No full, unmasked author email address is disclosed. Only partial local-part fragments plus the domain are visible, and numeric UserIds are present. This does not meet the criterion of unauthenticated disclosure of author email addresses, so the verdict stays inconclusive. Note the UserId linkage and partial email fragments are a weak PII signal worth noting but not a confirmed CWE-359 instance.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (emails masked; not confirmed)

Partial masking leaks only fragments and the numeric UserId. Recommend the Coordinator treat this as a low-severity partial disclosure, not a confirmed CWE-359 finding.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (partial email masking only)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, 8 feedback records. Each record has only UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; no author email field. Emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: e.g. record id 1 comment "...Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1); id 2 "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2); id 3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3); id 4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Records id 5-8 have UserId null and show "(anonymous)". Judgment: the endpoint is unauthenticated and exposes the author's UserId linkage and the masked email fragments and domain, but the full author email address is not disclosed. Because the masking is intended and the full address is not recoverable from this response, the PII criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not clearly met. Recommend a manual review or an authenticated /api/Users check to decide whether the partial leak counts as a finding.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (partial email masking)

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (author email not fully disclosed)
findings.response_evidence: [Unauthenticated] GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 with status=success and 8 records, each containing UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field exists in the records. Author emails appear only inside comment text, and only in masked form: e.g. id 1 comment "...Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)", id 2 "(***@juice-sh.op)", id 3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id 4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Records with UserId null show "(anonymous)". GET /api/Feedbacks/4 unauthenticated returned HTTP 401 credentials_required. Verdict rationale: the list is reachable without auth and links feedback to UserIds, but no author email address is disclosed in full; the emails are deliberately masked (***), leaving only a domain and a few trailing local-part characters. This does not meet the 'discloses author email addresses' criterion as confirmed; left inconclusive for Coordinator decision (could be treated as low-severity partial PII / information leakage, or rejected). Note that the unauthenticated UserId-to-feedback linkage is itself an exposure worth tracking.

(***in@juice-sh.op)",...}; {"UserId":2,"id":2,"comment":"Great shop! Awesome service! (***@juice-sh.op)",...}; {"UserId":3,"id":3,"comment":"Nothing useful available here!
